clue.text: Liverpudlian society needs firm handler

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm
a user is someone who handles or operates something

explanation.surface: A Liverpool club needs a firm person in charge of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scouser is the colloquial term for a native of Liverpool, after the local stew called scouse.

clue.text: Haggard heroine comes upon first religious Father to be a mountaineer

parts.note: She is the title heroine of H. Rider Haggard's novel

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A novelist's heroine meets a priest who is to become a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like worn-out; it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people famous as mountain guides and climbers.

clue.text: A specialist shop is opening

definitions.meaning: a shop selling a particular maker's goods

explanation.definitionFit: Outlet means both a retail store for particular goods and an opening that lets something escape.

clue.text: Frisky about being at university, maintaining a loyal interest

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: sportive means playful, frisky
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: A lively student keeps up a faithful concern for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Supportive describes someone who gives backing or encouragement, loyally interested.

clue.text: Europe has nothing to lose, changing currency

indicators.note: to lose means the letter for zero is taken out of the word
changing means the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the round symbol for zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Europe can afford no losses as it switches money.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from EUROPE leaves EURPE, which 'changing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the money of India, Pakistan and several other countries.

clue.text: Go quickly, wrapping redhead in topcoat

indicators.note: wrapping means the first piece goes round the second like a cover

parts.note: to vanish is to go away quickly, disappear
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry off, wrapping a red-haired person in an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topcoat' looks like a garment, but it is the final coat of finish on wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is applied as the final protective layer, the top coat, on furniture or woodwork.

clue.text: Choice articles from museum science room, including original urban man

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: including means the lab holds another letter inside

parts.note: a lab is a room for science work

indicators.note: original means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Les is a man's name

explanation.surface: Precious objects from a museum's laboratory include an early townsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuables are precious possessions, items chosen for their worth.

clue.text: Creature on soft slope

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, a creature
P, piano, is the music abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: An animal stands on a gentle incline.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined surface joining two levels.

clue.text: Little by little, male chin undergoes transformation

indicators.note: undergoes transformation means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man's jaw changes gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchmeal is an old word meaning gradually, inch by inch.

clue.text: Dance round trees by lake in Yorkshire

definitions.note: stands for a place in Yorkshire, a town name

indicators.note: round means the dance goes about the other pieces

parts.note: a hey is an old country dance
elms are trees

explanation.surface: People dance around trees beside a lake in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: HEY is an old country dance; HELMSLEY is a market town in North Yorkshire, with a ruined castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmsley is a market town in North Yorkshire, so it is found in that county.

clue.text: Hinder in law directions given to spinner

parts.note: E is the compass direction east
S is the compass direction south
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: Legal obstruction comes from instructions handed to a bowler who spins the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler; here it is the child's spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: I came bounding in, the parrot being disputatious

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the bird's name

parts.note: Poll, or Polly, is the stock name for a pet parrot

indicators.note: bounding, leaping about wildly, signals that these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bursts in while the parrot squawks argumentatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounding' reshuffles the letters of I CAME; Poll is the traditional name for a parrot, as Polly is.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing or speech is controversial and argumentative, given to dispute.

clue.text: Wonderful friend, capturing female to love to pieces

indicators.note: capturing means the friend holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a hen is a female bird
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A marvellous mate is captivated by a woman he loves to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pieces' reads as an idiom, but pieces are chessmen, MEN; both uses of 'to' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal is used informally for something remarkable or extraordinary.

clue.text: Writer mostly astray

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: amiss means wrong or gone astray

explanation.surface: An author has mostly lost his way.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis and his son Martin Amis are both well-known British novelists.

clue.text: Dog caught in lobster trap after son gets the bird

indicators.note: after means the trap and its contents follow the abbreviation
caught in means the dog sits inside the trap

parts.note: a creel is a basket trap for lobsters
a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog trapped in a lobster pot after a boy gets jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' is the idiom for being booed; here bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The screech owl is a species of owl named for its harsh cry.

clue.text: Greatly inclined to take Walesa as English by race

parts.note: steep means sharply sloping, greatly inclined
Lech Walesa is the Polish union leader and former president
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Polish leader, very keen, adopts the role of an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walesa' is fixed on as the surname, but only the first name LECH is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race over fences, or a track event with hurdles and a water jump.

clue.text: Mistaken and certain to be taken up about early duplicating machine

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the machine
taken up in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: sure means certain
Roneo was an early brand of stencil duplicator

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly believes an old copier is sure to be brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: Roneo was a trade name for a stencil duplicator used in offices before photocopiers, now dated, hence 'early'; 'taken up' suits a down clue, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means wrong, based on a mistake.

clue.text: Last drink? On your own head be it

definitions.meaning: a final alcoholic drink taken before bed

definitions.text: On your own head be it
definitions.meaning: read literally, a cap worn on the head in bed

explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is both a bedtime drink and a cloth cap once worn to bed.

clue.text: Surgeon who will do you if he can

definitions.text: who will do you if he can
definitions.meaning: to do someone is to swindle them, so a smooth trickster

explanation.definitionFit: Operator means one who operates, as a surgeon, and slang for a shrewd manipulator.

clue.text: Poor? I'm very old, retired, coming in chilled to the bone

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: coming in means the reversed letters go inside the next word

parts.note: perished is informal for extremely cold

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the pair of letters goes backwards

explanation.surface: A frail, elderly, retired person asks whether being frozen stiff makes him poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns V and O into OV, which goes after the P of PERISHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Impoverished means made poor, reduced to poverty.

clue.text: Wife having advantage over daughter gets stuck

parts.note: an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A wife who has the upper hand over her daughter gets trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the advantage above the daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedged means jammed tightly, stuck fast.

clue.text: Spirited witticism in heaven?

indicators.note: in means the joke goes inside the word for heaven

parts.note: the sky is the heavens
a pun is a witticism

explanation.surface: Is there any joking up in paradise?
explanation.definitionFit: Spunky means plucky, courageous and full of spirit.

clue.text: Wages heard to be up

indicators.note: heard means we want the word that is spoken the same

parts.note: something that is up is higher

explanation.surface: Pay is rumoured to be rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire is the payment for someone's services, as in the labourer is worthy of his hire.

clue.text: Distraught, he can't hope to get off lightly

indicators.note: distraught, wildly upset, signals that these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone frantic despairs of escaping with a light punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get off lightly' reads as escaping punishment; here lightly means at little cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the cheap means doing it for little expense, cheaply and lightly.

clue.text: Join companion on strike

indicators.note: in this down clue, on places the companion beneath the strike, so it comes second

parts.note: to hit is to strike
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A friend joins the workers' walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action, but it means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch is to fasten or join, as in hitching a trailer.

clue.text: Cast of beginners to see how everyone differs

indicators.note: beginners means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A theatre company of novices shows how people differ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a theatrical company; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off, as a snake casts its skin.

clue.text: Ruffian to get a division of the spoils (hot art, perhaps)

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings

indicators.note: perhaps means these letters are one possible arrangement of another word

explanation.surface: A thug gets his share of the loot, which may include stolen paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat is a murderer or violent criminal, a ruffian.

clue.text: Newspaper metaphor G and S take to heart

indicators.note: take to heart means the answer lies inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A journalist's figure of speech is taken seriously by Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.walkthrough: G and S looks like Gilbert and Sullivan, but the letters simply carry the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or periodical that speaks for a party or movement.

clue.text: Padre's a composer of marches

indicators.note: a composer of something puts it together, so these letters are assembled afresh

parts.note: the letters of the word as written, its S included

explanation.surface: An army chaplain writes military music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' suggests someone who writes music; here it rearranges PADRES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Parades are ceremonial processions, marches of troops or people.

clue.text: Divine, holding girl with time off

indicators.note: holding means the first word goes round the girl's name

parts.note: holy means divine, sacred
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A saintly figure holds a young woman while on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a period away from work, a break or vacation.
